invocations.why: The npm CLI bundles its required packages; declaring dependencies would make users install them separately.
AGENTS.md forbids comments in JS/TS code, and this check is what enforces it.
This is the lint gate itself. Without it nothing in .oxlintrc.json is enforced, and any extra path argument would narrow what gets linted.
AGENTS.md states that the agent-core-v2 layering, including the light remote executor, is enforced by this check.
The guards keep the oxlint config and the wiring of these checks from changing unnoticed.
It freezes rules that already have findings at their current count per file and reports suppressions that no longer suppress anything; without it new code could add to that debt unnoticed.
New tests must script models through the shared testkit; this check freezes the legacy model doubles at their current use per file so new cases cannot add to them.
AGENTS.md rules out sleep- and timeout-based synchronization in tests; this check freezes the existing fixed waits per test file so new code waits for a signal instead.

The old Desktop and TUI E2E directories no longer run on pull requests or main; this check freezes their test cases per file so a new case lands in tests/e2e, where it runs, instead of looking like coverage that nothing executes.
A quarantined Desktop journey must name an owner, a reason and an expiry date, and a protected or smoke journey can never be quarantined; without it a quarantine quietly becomes permanent.
Agents follow the paths and links in AGENTS.md files, and every session loads the root one; this check fails on a dead reference and keeps the root file within its byte budget.

The scenarios in tests/e2e are only worth trusting while their drivers reach the product the way a user does; this check keeps product internals, page and network backdoors, skips, retries, fixed waits and undocumented KIMI_* switches out of that directory.
This is where every L0 test in tests/protected.yaml must pass on its first attempt across the test shards; without it regression and contract IDs are listed but never enforced.
CI is the only place where lint blocks a merge; local runs and git hooks can be skipped.
The guards are code too. Their tests keep a broken guard from silently passing everything.
The comment check is code too. Its tests keep a broken check from silently passing every file.
Sherif keeps dependency versions and manifests consistent across the workspace.
The pre-commit hook gives the earliest lint feedback, before CI.
The pre-commit hook rejects comments in staged files before CI does.
The pre-commit hook lints staged files with the same rules CI enforces.
It keeps flake.nix in sync with the pnpm workspace; a package missing from flake.nix breaks the Nix build.

forbidden.why: lint-staged commits whatever its commands change. Some oxlint fixes change behavior (for example `unicorn/no-unnecessary-await` removes an `await`, which changes when the code after it runs), so the hook would rewrite code without telling anyone.

fanIn.why: It turns the L0 results of every test shard into one check. If it stopped waiting for the shards, or stopped running after a shard failed, a missing or failing L0 test would never be reported.

It reports every Desktop E2E shard under one check name. A job it does not wait for, or whose result it does not read, could fail while the check stays green. The nightly quarantine job is informational, and the alert job runs after it on main to keep the tracking issue, so both stay outside it.
